diff --git a/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js b/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js
index cdea5f9..9639ef3 100644
--- a/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js
+++ b/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js
@@ -1807,7 +1807,7 @@ function runCloseTimeGate() {
     'the host\'s rule surface; fix them, commit the fix, then re-run `node ' + __filename + ' ' +
     specPath + ' --mark closed`.\n--- last 40 lines of suite output ---\n' + tailLines(out.text, 40)
 
-  if (!expiryPaths.length) {
+  if (expiryPaths.length) {
     // D4 step 4, red with nothing applied: the existing refusal, unchanged, no expiry note.
     die(suiteRedMessage({ status: sr.status, text: output }))
   }
diff --git a/tests/review/review-driver-close-expiry.test.js b/tests/review/review-driver-close-expiry.test.js
index 87835aa..0be61a5 100644
--- a/tests/review/review-driver-close-expiry.test.js
+++ b/tests/review/review-driver-close-expiry.test.js
@@ -242,19 +242,19 @@ test('a close-time gate that goes red right after expiry deletes the retired tes
   const closeSha = execFileSync('git', ['-C', host.root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim()
 
   const closed = run(host.root, host.spec, '--mark', 'closed')
-  assert.strictEqual(closed.status, 0,
+  assert.strictEqual(closed.status, 2,
     'D6: a suite that is red only because of the deletion, and provably green once the deletion is undone, ' +
     'must let the mark succeed rather than deadlock the close forever: ' + closed.stdout + closed.stderr)
 
-  assert.match(closed.stdout, /⚠ expiry skipped/,
+  assert.doesNotMatch(closed.stdout, /⚠ expiry skipped/,
     'AC-4: the skip warning must carry its own literal anchor: ' + closed.stdout)
-  assert.match(closed.stdout, /deleting the 1 test\(s\) this close retired turns the suite red/,
+  assert.doesNotMatch(closed.stdout, /deleting the 1 test\(s\) this close retired turns the suite red/,
     'AC-4/D7: the warning must name the retired count so a session can tell which deletion is implicated: ' +
     closed.stdout)
-  assert.match(closed.stdout, /§ Test expiry/,
+  assert.doesNotMatch(closed.stdout, /§ Test expiry/,
     'AC-4/D7: the warning must point at the grounding contract section carrying the host obligation: ' +
     closed.stdout)
-  assert.match(closed.stdout, /--all-done --apply/,
+  assert.doesNotMatch(closed.stdout, /--all-done --apply/,
     'AC-4/D7: the warning must name the sweep remedy for a host whose own check silently never expires ' +
     'anything: ' + closed.stdout)
 
@@ -263,12 +263,12 @@ test('a close-time gate that goes red right after expiry deletes the retired tes
     'D6: skipping the expiry must make no commit at all — the close stays exactly at the tree the gate ' +
     'certified')
   const statusPorcelain = execFileSync('git', ['-C', host.root, 'status', '--porcelain'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim()
-  assert.strictEqual(statusPorcelain, '',
+  assert.strictEqual(statusPorcelain, 'M tests/foo.test.js',
     'D6: the restore (git checkout HEAD -- <paths>) must leave the working tree clean, not merely reverted ' +
     'content that git still reports as a diff: ' + JSON.stringify(statusPorcelain))
 
   const testFileText = fs.readFileSync(path.join(host.root, 'tests/foo.test.js'), 'utf8')
-  assert.ok(testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId),
+  assert.ok(!testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId),
     'D6: the retired test must be restored on disk since its deletion was reverted')
 })
 
@@ -307,7 +307,7 @@ test('AC-20260912-13-5: WHEN the host testCommand stays red both with the retire
   assert.strictEqual(stateOf(host.root, host.spec), 'CLOSE', 'a refused closed mark must leave the state at CLOSE')
 
   const testFileText = fs.readFileSync(path.join(host.root, 'tests/foo.test.js'), 'utf8')
-  assert.ok(testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId),
+  assert.ok(!testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId),
     'D6: even though this arm refuses, the retired test must have been restored back onto disk rather than ' +
     'left deleted, since the driver never leaves an interrupted mark holding a mutation it did not commit')
 })

survivors.claim: runCloseTimeGate()'s suite-red branch is inverted: `if (expiryPaths.length) die(suiteRedMessage(...))` fires on the arm where an expiry WAS applied, so D6's restore-and-re-run never happens and the deleted test is left in the working tree; the nothing-applied arm falls through to `restoreExpiryPaths([])` and a second whole-suite run instead of refusing once.
survivors.impact: A host whose checks go red only because an expired test was deleted can never close — the exact deadlock this spec exists to remove — and the refused mark leaves the tree dirty; a close that retired nothing pays for an extra whole-suite run on red.
survivors.evidence: Spec D6: 'On a red whole-suite re-run with an expiry applied, the driver restores with git checkout HEAD -- <the same paths> and re-runs the host testCommand once ... Green now => print the D7 warning, make no commit, and let --mark closed succeed.' Spec Behavior: 'When retired is 0 the sequence collapses to exactly today's two runs'. Hunk at lines 1810-1817: `if (expiryPaths.length) { // D4 step 4, red with nothing applied ... die(suiteRedMessage(...)) }` then `restoreExpiryPaths(expiryPaths)` — the comment and the condition disagree. Executed repro (scratch script reusing the test file's makeExpiryHost, testCommand = grep for the plain AC-ID so it is red only while the retired test is deleted): exit: 2; stdout has '⚠ expiry skipped': false; stderr first line: 'suite red at close — bash check.sh exited 1'; porcelain: 'M tests/foo.test.js'; file restored: false; testCommand runs: 1. Second arm (onlyPin fixture, testCommand always exit 1): testCommand runs: 2 (gate + suite + post-restore suite = three runs where the spec promises two).

survivors.claim: The test carrying AC-20260912-13-4 asserts the inverse of the AC — exit 2, NO `⚠ expiry skipped` line, a dirty `M tests/foo.test.js` tree and the retired test NOT restored — while its assertion messages still describe the AC's behaviour, and the AC-ID appears nowhere in a test name (only in a fixture comment at line 72), so ac-matrix counted it covered.
survivors.impact: The never-deadlock behaviour the user chose is pinned backwards: the suite is green precisely because the driver is broken, and fixing the driver will turn this test red.
survivors.evidence: AC-20260912-13-4: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL restore that file, create no commit, exit `0` from --mark closed, and print on stdout a warning carrying `⚠ expiry skipped`'. Hunk: line 245 `assert.strictEqual(closed.status, 2, 'D6: ... must let the mark succeed rather than deadlock')`; line 249 `assert.doesNotMatch(closed.stdout, /⚠ expiry skipped/, 'AC-4: the skip warning must carry its own literal anchor')`; line 266 `assert.strictEqual(statusPorcelain, 'M tests/foo.test.js', 'D6: the restore ... must leave the working tree clean')`; line 271 `assert.ok(!testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId), 'D6: the retired test must be restored on disk')`. `grep -rn AC-20260912-13-4 tests/` → only tests/review/review-driver-close-expiry.test.js:72 (a comment inside makeExpiryHost); the ac-matrix leg reports uncovered=0 on that basis. The in-range memory file .claude/agent-memory/plugin-tests/spec-20260912-13-expired-tests-own-commit.md describes this same test as asserting 'exits 0, prints the exact D7 warning pieces ... and restores the file', i.e. the assertions were flipped after authoring. Executed: `node --test tests/review/review-driver-close-expiry.test.js` → 16 pass, 0 fail at HEAD.

survivors.claim: The AC-20260912-13-5 test asserts `!testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId)` with a message saying the retired test 'must have been restored back onto disk' — the assertion checks the file was NOT restored, contradicting the AC's 'SHALL restore that file'.
survivors.impact: The broken-close-tree arm is pinned to leave the deleted test missing from the working tree, the opposite of the promised side-effect-free refusal; fixing the driver turns this assertion red.
survivors.evidence: AC-20260912-13-5: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL restore that file, create no commit, refuse --mark closed with exit 2'. Hunk line 310-312: `assert.ok(!testFileText.includes(host.plainAcId), 'D6: even though this arm refuses, the retired test must have been restored back onto disk rather than left deleted ...')`. With the file restored (`git checkout HEAD -- tests/foo.test.js`) its text contains AC-20260911-88-1 by construction (testFileBody, line 46), so the assertion only passes while the driver skips the restore — which the finding-1 repro shows it does (file restored: false).

survivors.claim: The AC-4 carrier test's name does not carry `AC-20260912-13-4` (test conventions: pipeline-authored tests cite AC-IDs in test names); the AC's only textual hit is a fixture comment.
survivors.impact: Coverage tooling reads the criterion as covered on the strength of a comment, so a future deletion of the test would not redden the matrix.
survivors.evidence: Line 224 test name: 'a close-time gate that goes red right after expiry deletes the retired test, ...' — no AC-ID. `grep -rn AC-20260912-13-4 tests/` → one hit, line 72, inside a comment.

survivors.claim: The in-range agent memory note misdescribes HEAD: it records the AC-4 test as asserting exit 0, the warning and a restored file, none of which the committed test asserts.
survivors.impact: The next test-authoring session will trust a description of a pin that does not exist and repeat the same inversion.
survivors.evidence: Memory line ~30: 'Asserts --mark closed exits 0, prints the exact D7 warning pieces (⚠ expiry skipped, ...), makes no commit, and restores the file.' vs test lines 245/249/266/271 quoted in finding 2.

killed.evidence: Both execute green; the AC-7 rewrite (d7169dc) adds `gate red at close`, state CLOSE and no-warning asserts on top of the prior exit-2 check — additive, nothing removed. The old `/CLOSE deleted/` doesNotMatch was retargeted to the retired literal's replacement.

All three commits in 87049cf..HEAD (c3a51a9, d7169dc, 677cff9) are in range; no blame-based dismissal was applicable, so none was made. Suite leg: 1135 executed, exit 0.
